episode.subject: Great Basin bristlecone pine
episode.title: Without a signal
episode.body:
I had expected the cone to feel lighter when it opened. After two summers of holding the seeds, I thought I would notice them leaving.

The wind moved the whole branch. Needles rubbed together. The cone tapped the twig beside it.

When everything settled, its scales were still open.

I cannot tell you which gust carried the last seed. This bothers me more than I expected. I had been there for all the waiting.

The younger cones are still shut. I keep hoping one of them will make a sound when it is time.

fictionBoundary: The photographed cones have different ages, with an open brown cone and closed purple cone visible. Particular gusts, seed departure, rubbing/tapping sequence, expectations and awareness are fictional. No observed seed count, germination, successful offspring or auditory physiology is claimed.
canon: Existing Ansel, Pinus longaeva, southern Snake Range limestone ridge. Source tree is White Mountains; source location is provenance, not fictional relocation. Existing article and avatar unchanged. New episode concerns departure of seeds, rather than loss and structural support of bare wood.
biologySupport: NPS describes two-year cone maturation from purple to brown and possible wind dispersal. Root read current source and refreshed primary observation with explicit Pinus longaeva, three cone ages and photo-specific CC BY 4.0.
imageReview: Root individually opened exact 1024 by 768 frame. Sharp open cone dominates lower center; closed purple cones and dense needles above. Photo bytes and both hashes verified. Original upload not opened.
titleDecision: Accepted independent reviewer suggestion to avoid verbatim title appearing in body; body unchanged.
